title: Grok and the trail back to a post
summary: Grok can find what an organization said on X. A post, its date, and the policy behind it are three different pieces of evidence.

intro.what: Grok is xAI’s assistant and model family. It is useful when the source you need is a public statement on X.
intro.features: Depending on the product and enabled tools, it can search public posts or the web, interpret images and return text. Grok Imagine provides separate image and video generation.
intro.exchange: Trace a widely shared mail-delay claim to its original post and timestamp. Confirm tenant impact in your own service-health records.
intro.m365: Identify who announced a feature and then look up its rollout, license and platform in Microsoft’s documentation.
intro.developer: Find public reactions to a feature idea or try Imagine for a cover. Inspect the original feedback and the exported artwork.

sections.title: Trace a claim to the speaker
paragraphs: Suppose someone says a cruise line changed embarkation times. Ask for posts from the official account within the sailing month. Require the post link, publication date, port and sailing date. Open the link. Then compare the wording with the passenger notice. A genuine post announcing a trial in one port can still be poor evidence for a fleetwide rule.

In an application using Grok, X Search and Web Search are tools the developer can enable. X Search is a good fit for recovering the original announcement. Web Search is useful for finding the operator’s policy page. A plain model call that has neither tool gets neither source of fresh information.

sections.title: Choose an output before choosing a model
paragraphs: Grok 4.7 accepts text and images and returns text through the API. The model has a 500,000-token context window and adjustable reasoning effort. Start with a compact request to extract the text of a sign. Increase effort for a reconciliation of conflicting notices and inspect which one has the later effective date.

Grok Imagine has separate engines for creating images and video. For a clip, supply a reference frame and describe one motion. For a spoken interface, investigate the Grok Voice family. These choices matter if the deliverable is an image file, a playable clip or a voice conversation.

title: Perplexity and Comet
summary: Start with a question in Perplexity or bring the assistant to the pages you already have open in Comet.

intro.what: Perplexity is a research assistant with linked sources. Comet is its browser, which can bring an assistant into a browsing session.
intro.features: Search can lead back to source pages. Comet can use browsing context, and the Agent API exposes tools for developers building search into an application.
intro.exchange: Find the current documentation for a message-trace field, then verify its meaning against the field reference and your own export.
intro.m365: Compare published admin instructions across two versions. Open both sources and check the applicable license and release date.
intro.developer: Use the API when the app needs sourced, current answers. For an offline reference book, save reviewed material in the edition.
sources: Perplexity · Sonar and the Agent API

sections.title: Audit an answer with citations
paragraphs: For a research question, ask Perplexity to find the original document and give its publication and effective dates. For example, ask which transit agency publishes the timetable for a particular airport station. In the cited PDF, check the direction, day of week and date. A source can mention the station without supporting the departure time in the answer.

For developers, the Agent API combines model selection with tools such as web search and URL fetching. Perplexity ended support for Sonar Chat Completions on September 27, 2026. The migration guide describes forwarding for synchronous and streaming requests and a move to background mode for asynchronous work. Older Sonar examples deserve a date check.
sources: Perplexity · Sonar and the Agent API

sections.title: Use the browser for work across pages
paragraphs: Comet is Perplexity’s browser, available on desktop and mobile, including iOS. Consider comparing two hotels with their cancellation policies open. Ask the assistant to extract the deadline, local time zone, deposit and fee for each reservation. Open each cited rate condition yourself before booking. An aggregator’s generic cancellation page may describe a different rate.

Decide which tabs a task needs. Comet’s privacy controls describe the information shared when its assistant needs personal browsing context. Use the device’s own controls to check permissions and feature availability. A desktop walkthrough can show controls that are arranged differently on the iPad.

title: Mistral, Gemma and running a model locally
summary: A specialist for recorded speech and a model you can run on your own hardware solve different problems. Here is how to try each.

intro.what: Mistral Vibe is an assistant for work and code. Voxtral is an audio model family. Gemma is Google’s family of downloadable models that can run on compatible hardware.
intro.features: Vibe offers chat and coding sessions. Voxtral models support specialized speech tasks. Gemma lets a developer choose the local runtime, model size and hardware.
intro.exchange: A local model can summarize an approved, sanitized mail-flow example. Check the event order against the export and confirm the runtime stays local.
intro.m365: Test transcription of synthetic meeting audio for names and speaker changes before considering it for a documentation workflow.
intro.developer: Try a small local model for searchable personal notes. Put the device offline and measure startup time and memory with a real file.
sources: Google · Gemma 4 models and memory requirements

sections.title: A specialist for voice or code
paragraphs: Mistral Vibe, formerly Le Chat, is the company’s assistant for work and coding. Its product page distinguishes chat from coding sessions. For recorded speech, the Voxtral family offers specialized audio capabilities. Check the model’s supported languages and direction of conversion before selecting it.

For a recorded bilingual meeting, transcribe a one-minute sample containing names, overlaps and a switch in language. Mark omissions and misattributed speakers. A fluent written summary can conceal mistakes made during transcription.

sections.title: Run inference without a network
paragraphs: Google’s Gemma family offers downloadable model weights. Weights are the learned numerical parameters. A compatible inference application loads those weights and runs the model on your device. Google’s Gemma 4 guide lists model sizes, input types and memory estimates. The weights, runtime, context length and working memory must all fit the hardware.

For a flight, download the model and runtime before leaving. Disable the network, relaunch, and try a fresh prompt against a locally saved document. Check whether the application quietly uses an online service for search, speech or document extraction. Downloading this field guide saves its chapters. Running a local AI requires a separate setup.
sources: Google · Gemma 4 models and memory requirements

title: Chrome add-ins and AI browsers
summary: A chat tab, a built-in browser assistant and an extension can see different things, even if they use a related model.

intro.what: A browser assistant uses information from a page or tab. It can be built into the browser, as with Gemini in Chrome or Comet, or supplied by an extension such as Claude in Chrome.
intro.features: Depending on the tool, it can summarize the current page, compare shared tabs or interact with controls. Desktop Chrome offers site-access settings for extensions.
intro.exchange: Compare two public troubleshooting articles side by side. Share only the pages you intend and verify the applicability to your Exchange version.
intro.m365: Use it to read policy documentation. An assistant operating a signed-in admin page may be able to take real actions with that identity.
intro.developer: Preview a personal app in a test profile. Give the assistant a concrete layout to inspect and repeat the check on iPad.
sources: Chrome Help · manage extension site access

sections.title: Identify what has access
paragraphs: If a passenger-fare PDF is open in another tab, a plain chat only has the material you give it or that its own tools can reach. A built-in assistant may be able to use a shared tab. A desktop extension can request access to selected websites and, depending on the extension, interact with their controls. Comet provides an assistant within its own browser.

In desktop Chrome, open the extension’s details and inspect site access. Where supported, limit access to a click or specific sites. If all a task needs is one paragraph, selecting it and pasting it into a chat makes the input easy to inspect. Read what a tool plans to submit before letting it act in a signed-in account.
sources: Chrome Help · manage extension site access

sections.title: Match the instructions to your device
paragraphs: On a desktop, Chrome Web Store extensions can add a side panel or page controls. Chrome’s phone option to add an extension to desktop queues it for your computer. On iPad, begin with the provider’s supported app or browser and check its mobile instructions.

Quick test: open two public pages with different opening hours. Ask for one row per page and the source URL for each. A correct answer that only quotes the active tab tells you something about that setup. Repeat with the second page explicitly shared before judging the underlying model.
sources: Chrome Help · manage extension site access
